what_happened: Job 20261111-064834-q749 (a code job to refuse readings that defer a numbered request part or Acceptance bullet) failed in planning, before any code was written. After the last round (5 of 5) the critic still said the plan needed revising. One major finding blocked it: about twenty drain tests queue requests through the helper queue_steward_request (drain.rs:2573-2601). That helper adds the three standard Steward bullets. The Scenario::default() and rated_scenario() readings those tests use do not cover two of the bullets: 'fmt, clippy and test pass' and 'The change is made as described: ...'. The new gate would refuse them and break assertions such as report.landed == 1. The plan did not list these tests as dependents and wrongly said the rated_scenario tests need no change, so criterion 8 could not be shown as planned. Four minor findings were also raised: three test files (job_plan.rs, drain.rs, proposals.rs) are not among the reading's deliverables; real readers are not told the coverage convention up front; the gate is a stack of hand-tuned heuristics with known false positives and negatives; and the plan cites wrong lines for structural_text and does not pin sibling-stem behaviour. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named files and seams exist, but nothing makes the plan run a new refusal rule over every existing caller and fixture that feeds it. The standard Steward bullets are added automatically by a shared test helper. The plan did not trace that helper to the drain tests whose canned readings cannot cover those bullets. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so one major finding left at round 5 loses all planning spend. The job is a narrower retry of the earlier attempt on the same request (20261029-212839-tcjb). Its dependents survey still missed the generated-bullet path through the test helpers.
other_causes: The plan's deliverable list was not reconciled with the test files it needed to touch (job_plan.rs, drain.rs, proposals.rs), so the reading and the plan disagreed on scope.
The gate depends on hand-tuned lexical heuristics, so the real effect on existing fixtures is hard to predict without running it.
open_hypotheses: Whether a plan that ran the gate over all drain test scenarios in round 1 would have converged within 5 rounds is not shown by the fields.
Whether the tests should be fixed by giving each scenario its own covering bullet or by resizing the verdicts is not settled by the fields.
contradictions: The critic said the plan fits the reading, its seams exist, and its claims about job_plan.rs, proposals.rs, the fake reader and the fake verifier hold up. The only blocker was the missed drain-test dependents, so most of the planning was sound.
prevention: When a plan adds a refusal or matching rule, Athena should run a mechanical replay before the critic rounds. The replay should run the new rule over every existing test helper and scenario that reaches it, plus recorded real request shapes, and list the ones it would newly refuse. The plan must list those as dependents and handle them, for example by giving each scenario a bullet-covering reading. The same replay would have caught this in round 1 and the earlier attempt's invented-bullet gap. A repair or partial-plan path for a single remaining major finding would also stop the loss of all planning spend.
proposed_request: Refuse readings that defer a numbered request part or Acceptance bullet. Outcome: a reading that leaves out or defers a numbered part or an Acceptance bullet of the request is refused with a message naming the part. Requests that Steward generates, with its three standard bullets, must still be accepted when the reading covers them. Include the existing tests in your scope: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (the queue_steward_request helper at about lines 2573-2601 and the roughly twenty tests that use it with Scenario::default() or rated_scenario() readings), job_plan.rs and proposals.rs. Make those scenario readings cover the three standard bullets ('fmt, clippy and test pass', 'The change is made as described: <title>' and the third) so assertions such as report.landed == 1 still hold. Acceptance: (1) a reading that drops a numbered part is refused; (2) a reading that defers a part to a follow-up is refused; (3) the real standard Steward bullets, copied from steward.rs, are accepted when covered; (4) every existing drain test passes unchanged in what it asserts; (5) fmt, clippy and test pass; (6) a CHANGELOG.md entry is added.
